match_nodes_bipartite(pred_nodes: dict, gt_nodes: dict, max_dist: float = 7.0):\n    pred_by_t: dict[int, list[int]] = {}\n    for pid, (t, *_r) in pred_nodes.items():\n Cell tracking pipeline — overview\n\nThis notebook tracks cells through a 3D microscope movie in two learned stages plus a rule-based finisher:\n\n1. **Detect** — a 3D temporal U-Net (`TemporalUNet3D`) turns the raw movie into a per-voxel cell-center heatmap; NMS + a sigmoid threshold extract one **point per cell** per frame.\n2. **Link** — a transformer (`SimpleNodeTransformer`) scores every candidate connection between consecutive frames; an ILP solver picks the globally optimal set of links (each cell ≤ 1 parent, ≤ 2 children), forming **divisions** natively.\n3. **Finish** — a DeepCenter center-prior model vetoes false divisions, and a geometry-based safe-division rule confirms real ones.\n\nThe scored metric is `adjusted_edge_jaccard + 0.1 · division_jaccard` under a 7µm bipartite match. The bottleneck is **detection in crowded / division-heavy frames** (where divisions happen); cleaner candidate points are the main lever for a higher score.","metadata":{}},{"cell_type":"markdown","source":"# 1. Detector — `TemporalUNet3D`\n\nMaps the raw movie `(B, T, 1, Z, Y, X)` to a 32-channel feature map `(B, T, 32, Z, Y, X)`; a `Conv3d(32→1)` head gives one **cell-center logit per voxel** (the heatmap).\n\n**U-Net (encoder → decoder + skips).** Each stage is two 3×3×3 convolutions with BatchNorm + ReLU:\n\n$$\\text{block}(x)=\\mathrm{ReLU}\\big(\\mathrm{BN}(W_2 * \\mathrm{ReLU}(\\mathrm{BN}(W_1 * x)))\\big)$$\n\nA 3D conv $W*x$ makes each output voxel a learned weighted sum of its $3^3{=}27$ neighbours; stacking these + `MaxPool3d(2)` between stages (widths 32→64→128) grows the receptive field. The decoder `Upsample(×2)` **concatenates the matching encoder map** (skip connection), fusing coarse \"a cell is around here\" with fine \"exactly this voxel\" — enabling precise localization.\n\n**Temporal attention.** After each stage, every spatial location attends to itself across the `T` frames:\n\n$$\\mathrm{Attention}(Q,K,V)=\\mathrm{softmax}\\!\\Big(\\tfrac{QK^\\top}{\\sqrt{d}}\\Big)V,\\qquad x\\leftarrow x+\\mathrm{attn}(x)$$\n\nso motion/persistence across time reinforces real cells and suppresses flicker.\n\nAt inference we run a dual-seed ensemble (two checkpoints) blended in **probability space** (secondary detection weight `sdw`), then NMS + threshold to points.","metadata":{}},{"cell_type":"markdown","source":"# 2. Edge scorer — `SimpleNodeTransformer`\n\nGiven detected **points** with 33-dim features per frame, it scores every candidate link between frame $t$ and $t{+}1$: output = edge-logit matrix $(N_t, N_{t+1})$.\n\n- Project features to 128-dim, then **4 bi-directional cross-attention blocks**: $t$-nodes attend to $t{+}1$-nodes and vice-versa ($q \\leftarrow q + \\mathrm{CrossAttn}(q,k)$, $k \\leftarrow k + \\mathrm{CrossAttn}(k,q)$), each `LayerNorm → MHA → residual → MLP(GELU) → residual`. This makes each cell's embedding **context-aware** — key for disambiguating crowded regions.\n- A **pairwise MLP** scores $[q_i, k_j, (\\text{coord}_i-\\text{coord}_j)/100]$ → one logit $=P(\\text{link})$. The relative-position term encodes \"cells don't teleport.\"\n- A separate **ForkHead** scores a *triple* $(\\text{parent}, d_1, d_2)$ jointly → $P(\\text{division})$, since the pairwise MLP can never see both daughters at once.\n\n**Linking:** edge logits → sigmoid → an **ILP solver** with appearance/disappearance/division costs picks the globally optimal links and forms divisions; a DeepCenter veto + safe-division geometry rule finish the tracks.\n\n**Metric loss family (training):** the detector head is trained with weighted binary cross-entropy $\\mathcal{L}=-\\sum_v w_v[y_v\\log\\sigma(\\ell_v)+(1-y_v)\\log(1-\\sigma(\\ell_v))]$ against a per-voxel cell-center target.","metadata":{}},{"cell_type":"markdown","source":"## 936 — secondary_edge_weight 0.15 (banked config; 0.20 fork实测0.935)\n\n**Hypothesis (v16):** 0.20 fork 实测 0.935 < banked 0.936, 回退 0.15 单旋钮配置.\n\n**Everything else is IDENTICAL to 946** (det0.965, app0/disapp2, bidir0.15, sdw0.80, DeepCenter veto ON, gap2 + rescue + safe-div ON).\n\n**Pre-registered promotion rule:** ACCEPT (keep as new base) iff LB > 0.936. Reproducing\nthem today does not give you 0.966, and this notebook shows why: they exploited a\nproperty of the division metric that the organisers removed on 2026-07-17.\n\nIt then measures the thing that is actually blocking the division term now, on all\n199 training videos, on CPU, in about thirty seconds.\n\n**What is in here**\n\n1. What the exploit was, and the commit that closed it\n2. A gate audit over every ground-truth division in the training set — 151 of them\n3. What that says about where the remaining division score is\n\nPredictions are cached from my own GPU kernel; this notebook re-runs no inference,\nso it forks and runs on CPU in minutes.","id":"c13"},{"cell_type":"markdown","metadata":{},"source":"## 1. The exploit\n\nThe 0.963 and 0.966 notebooks differ in six lines. Two of them matter:\n\n```\n- MAX_COMPONENTS = 1400        + MAX_COMPONENTS = 3000\n- FORKS = 5                    + FORKS = 20\n```\n\nThose feed an `augment_dataset()` step that appends synthetic rows to the\nsubmission:\n\n```python\nhub_id = next_id                       # t = -1000, (z, y, x) = (-10000, -10000, -10000)\nnew_edges = [row(dataset, \"edge\", source_id=hub_id, target_id=root)\n             for root in roots]        # roots = the largest MAX_COMPONENTS tracks\n\nfor index in range(FORKS):             # a chain of FORKS fake divisions\n    new_edges += [\n        row(dataset, \"edge\", source_id=previous_id,  target_id=divider_id),\n        row(dataset, \"edge\", source_id=divider_id,   target_id=child_id),\n        row(dataset, \"edge\", source_id=divider_id,   target_id=continuation_id),\n    ]\n```\n\nOne hub node outside the volume, wired to the root of every track, plus a chain of\nfake forks. Nothing near a real cell.\n\n**Why it worked.** The division metric at the time required, for a ground-truth\ndivision to count as a true positive:\n\n> - **Single connected component.** All the matched predicted nodes above lie in\n>   one connected component of the predicted graph.\n> - **Contains a predicted fork.** The component includes at least one predicted\n>   dividing node (a predicted cell with two outgoing edges).\n\nThe hub merges every track into one weakly connected component, satisfying the\nfirst clause for every division at once. The fake forks satisfy the second. So any\nground-truth division whose parent and both daughters were merely *detected*\nscored as a true positive. The division Jaccard goes to roughly 1.0, and it is\nweighted 0.1 — which is most of the distance from 0.866 to 0.966.\n\n**Why it no longer works.**\n\n```\n2026-07-17  aa65e90  updating metric to patch weakly connected component exploit\n2026-06-26  b7a6192  Initial public release\n```\n\n`metrics.md` now reads, in as many words:\n\n> Merely sharing a weakly connected component is not sufficient.\n\nThe rule is local: the fork must be the matched parent or its immediate successor,\nand the two daughters must land on two distinct direct-child branches of that fork.\nA hub at t = -1000 is not the immediate predecessor of anything real.\n\nThose leaderboard entries are fossils of the old metric. The scores stand; the\nmethod does not reproduce.","id":"c14"},{"cell_type":"markdown","metadata":{},"source":"## 2. What this does and does not buy you\n\nOpening both gates roughly triples how many real divisions are even *reachable*.\nThat is a necessary condition, not a sufficient one — I tested it end to end on\nheld-out videos with the official metric and the score went **down**:\n\n| arm | forks proposed | division TP/FP/FN | adj edge Jaccard | score |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| gates as shipped (2.25 / 0.6) | 145 | 1 / 1 / 6 | 0.9383 | **0.9508** |\n| gates open (−999 / off) | 541 | 0 / 19 / 7 | 0.9341 | 0.9341 |\n| middle (0.0 / 1.2) | 541 | 0 / 17 / 7 | 0.9354 | 0.9354 |\n\nOpening the gates takes the candidate pool from 141 to 1,586 in one video, and\n`cap_skipped` goes from 0 to 43. The per-frame budget is about five slots and the\nranking key is `parent_dist + 0.15 * sister_dist` sorted ascending — pure geometry,\ntightest pair first. Tightest pairs are duplicate detections, not divisions. The\nbudget gets spent before a real division is reached, and the one true positive that\nexisted is lost.\n\n**So the binding constraint is the ranking, not the gates.** Anything that scores a\ncandidate fork on evidence rather than on how close the two points are should\nrecover this, and the gates have to come open at the same time or there is nothing\nto rank.\n\nOne more thing worth knowing if you are tuning divisions: the offline division\nmetric in the widely-forked public stack is **not** the official one. Cell tracking pipeline — overview\n\nThis notebook tracks cells through a 3D microscope movie in two learned stages plus a rule-based finisher:\n\n1. **Detect** — a 3D temporal U-Net (`TemporalUNet3D`) turns the raw movie into a per-voxel cell-center heatmap; NMS + a sigmoid threshold extract one **point per cell** per frame.\n2. **Link** — a transformer (`SimpleNodeTransformer`) scores every candidate connection between consecutive frames; an ILP solver picks the globally optimal set of links (each cell ≤ 1 parent, ≤ 2 children), forming **divisions** natively.\n3. **Finish** — a DeepCenter center-prior model vetoes false divisions, and a geometry-based safe-division rule confirms real ones.\n\nThe scored metric is `adjusted_edge_jaccard + 0.1 · division_jaccard` under a 7µm bipartite match. The bottleneck is **detection in crowded / division-heavy frames** (where divisions happen); cleaner candidate points are the main lever for a higher score.","metadata":{}},{"cell_type":"markdown","source":"# 1. Detector — `TemporalUNet3D`\n\nMaps the raw movie `(B, T, 1, Z, Y, X)` to a 32-channel feature map `(B, T, 32, Z, Y, X)`; a `Conv3d(32→1)` head gives one **cell-center logit per voxel** (the heatmap).\n\n**U-Net (encoder → decoder + skips).** Each stage is two 3×3×3 convolutions with BatchNorm + ReLU:\n\n$$\\text{block}(x)=\\mathrm{ReLU}\\big(\\mathrm{BN}(W_2 * \\mathrm{ReLU}(\\mathrm{BN}(W_1 * x)))\\big)$$\n\nA 3D conv $W*x$ makes each output voxel a learned weighted sum of its $3^3{=}27$ neighbours; stacking these + `MaxPool3d(2)` between stages (widths 32→64→128) grows the receptive field. The decoder `Upsample(×2)` **concatenates the matching encoder map** (skip connection), fusing coarse \"a cell is around here\" with fine \"exactly this voxel\" — enabling precise localization.\n\n**Temporal attention.** After each stage, every spatial location attends to itself across the `T` frames:\n\n$$\\mathrm{Attention}(Q,K,V)=\\mathrm{softmax}\\!\\Big(\\tfrac{QK^\\top}{\\sqrt{d}}\\Big)V,\\qquad x\\leftarrow x+\\mathrm{attn}(x)$$\n\nso motion/persistence across time reinforces real cells and suppresses flicker.\n\nAt inference we run a dual-seed ensemble (two checkpoints) blended in **probability space** (secondary detection weight `sdw`), then NMS + threshold to points.","metadata":{}},{"cell_type":"markdown","source":"# 2. Edge scorer — `SimpleNodeTransformer`\n\nGiven detected **points** with 33-dim features per frame, it scores every candidate link between frame $t$ and $t{+}1$: output = edge-logit matrix $(N_t, N_{t+1})$.\n\n- Project features to 128-dim, then **4 bi-directional cross-attention blocks**: $t$-nodes attend to $t{+}1$-nodes and vice-versa ($q \\leftarrow q + \\mathrm{CrossAttn}(q,k)$, $k \\leftarrow k + \\mathrm{CrossAttn}(k,q)$), each `LayerNorm → MHA → residual → MLP(GELU) → residual`. This makes each cell's embedding **context-aware** — key for disambiguating crowded regions.\n- A **pairwise MLP** scores $[q_i, k_j, (\\text{coord}_i-\\text{coord}_j)/100]$ → one logit $=P(\\text{link})$. The relative-position term encodes \"cells don't teleport.\"\n- A separate **ForkHead** scores a *triple* $(\\text{parent}, d_1, d_2)$ jointly → $P(\\text{division})$, since the pairwise MLP can never see both daughters at once.\n\n**Linking:** edge logits → sigmoid → an **ILP solver** with appearance/disappearance/division costs picks the globally optimal links and forms divisions; a DeepCenter veto + safe-division geometry rule finish the tracks.\n\n**Metric loss family (training):** the detector head is trained with weighted binary cross-entropy $\\mathcal{L}=-\\sum_v w_v[y_v\\log\\sigma(\\ell_v)+(1-y_v)\\log(1-\\sigma(\\ell_v))]$ against a per-voxel cell-center target.","metadata":{}},{"cell_type":"markdown","source":"## 948 — secondary_edge_weight 0.15 → 0.20 (single-knob tune off banked 0.936 / 946)\n\n**Hypothesis:** raising the secondary model's edge-logit weight in the harmonic fusion (0.15→0.20) gives the second seed slightly more say in edge scoring, which may recover a few correct links the primary alone under-scores.\n\n**Everything else is IDENTICAL to 946** (det0.965, app0/disapp2, bidir0.15, sdw0.80, DeepCenter veto ON, gap2 + rescue + safe-div ON).\n\n**Pre-registered promotion rule:** ACCEPT (keep as new base) iff LB > 0.936. Public LB. The core tracking architecture remains unchanged throughout — same UNet3D + node-transformer framework, dual-seed ensemble, ILP-based global linking, harmonic bidirectional association, repair pipeline, and held-out post-process selection. The **0.934 → 0.939** step widened safe division recovery while making bidirectional association more conservative. The **0.939 → 0.941** step redistributed the repair budget by widening the safe-division parent search while tightening its learned confirmation and gap closing. The **0.941 → 0.946** step extended the existing eight-view spatial TTA from detection outputs into the primary UNet features used for association. This **0.946 → 0.947** step keeps that primary feature ensemble intact and extends spatial ensembling into two remaining model-dependent paths: the secondary model's association features and the DeepCenter repair gate, together with a small retuning of the DeepCenter safe-division threshold from 0.25 to 0.20.\n\n| Component | 0.934 | 0.939 | 0.941 | 0.946 | 0.947 |\n| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |\n| Safe division parent max distance | 7.0 µm | 7.0 µm | 9.0 µm | 9.0 µm | 9.0 µm |\n| Safe division sister max distance | 12.0 µm | 14.0 µm | 14.0 µm | 14.0 µm | 14.0 µm |\n| Sister symmetry gate | off | 0.6 | 0.6 | 0.6 | 0.6 |\n| DeepCenter safe-division veto | off | on | on | on | on |\n| DeepCenter safe-division threshold | 0.12 | 0.12 | 0.25 | 0.25 | 0.20 |\n| DeepCenter spatial TTA | off | off | off | off | on |\n| Gap-close base radius | 5.8 µm | 5.8 µm | 5.0 µm | 5.0 µm | 5.0 µm |\n| Bidirectional association weight | 0.30 | 0.15 | 0.15 | 0.15 | 0.15 |\n| Bidirectional winner-agreement guard | on | removed | removed | removed | removed |\n| DeepCenter expected epoch | 500 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 |\n| Detection spatial TTA views | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 |\n| Primary edge-feature spatial TTA | off | off | off | on | on |\n| Secondary edge-feature spatial TTA | off | off | off | off | on |\n| Secondary edge-feature TTA weight | - | - | - | - | 0.75 |\n| Held-out post-process selection | off | off | off | on | on |\n\n**Recap: wider division search with a symmetry and DeepCenter guard (0.934 → 0.939).** The sister-distance limit widened from 12 µm to 14 µm to recover genuine divisions where the two daughters had drifted slightly farther apart. Since a wider radius alone also admits more spurious pairings, two safeguards compensate: a symmetry gate rejecting daughter candidates sitting at very uneven distances from the parent,\n\n$$\n\\frac{|d_1 - d_2|}{(d_1 + d_2)/2} \\le 0.6\n$$\n\nand the DeepCenter veto, so every candidate the wider geometric search proposes still needs independent confirmation before being accepted.\n\n**Recap: a more conservative bidirectional fusion (0.934 → 0.939).** Association is normally scored only forward in time — for a cell at frame $t$, which detection at $t+1$ it most likely became. This pipeline also scores it in reverse — given a detection at $t+1$, which detection at $t$ it most likely came from. Let $p_f$ be the forward probability and $p_r$ the reverse probability for a candidate pair. The reverse weight dropped from 0.30 to 0.15, so $p_r$ acts as a lighter supporting vote rather than pulling $p_f$ as strongly, and the previous requirement that forward and reverse agree on the exact same winner was removed. Their mutual support is instead represented through the harmonic probability:\n\n$$\np_{\\text{harmonic}} = \\frac{2 \\, p_f \\, p_r}{p_f + p_r}\n$$\n\nThis preserves the idea that a strong temporal link should receive support from both temporal directions without imposing a hard winner-agreement requirement.\n\n**Recap: redistributing the repair budget (0.939 → 0.941).** The association setup that reached 0.939 is left untouched; three repair-stage parameters are retuned instead. The safe-division **parent** radius increases from 7 µm to 9 µm. This is a different axis from the earlier 12 → 14 µm change — that one widened the allowed distance *between the two daughters*; this one widens the distance *from the parent to the missing daughter candidate*, recovering parent-child links the previous radius was cutting off. That wider parent search creates more room for false division proposals, so the DeepCenter confirmation threshold is raised from 0.12 to 0.25. Candidates admitted by the larger radius still have to clear a stricter learned confirmation before being recovered as divisions. At the same time, gap closing is tightened, with its base radius reduced from 5.8 µm to 5.0 µm. Together these changes move more repair capacity toward plausible divisions while tightening independent confirmation and gap recovery elsewhere.\n\n**Recap: extending the primary spatial ensemble into association features (0.941 → 0.946).** The 0.941 pipeline already evaluates detection using the full eight spatial transformations of the D4 symmetry group. The 0.946 change does not increase the number of transformations. Instead, it extends the same transform-invert-average principle from detection logits into the primary UNet feature tensor consumed by the edge predictor. The eight spatial views are:\n\n| No. | D4 Spatial View | Operation |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| 1 | Identity | Original orientation |\n| 2 | Horizontal flip | Reflection across one spatial axis |\n| 3 | Vertical flip | Reflection across the other spatial axis |\n| 4 | Horizontal + vertical flip | Reflection across both axes, equivalent to a 180° rotation |\n| 5 | Rotation 90° | 90° spatial rotation |\n| 6 | Rotation 270° | 270° spatial rotation |\n| 7 | Transpose | Reflection across one diagonal |\n| 8 | Anti-transpose | Reflection across the opposite diagonal |\n\nFor an input $x$, let $T_i$ denote the $i$-th D4 transformation. Detection logits are aligned back into the original coordinate system and averaged:\n\n$$\n\\bar{L}(x) = \\frac{1}{8}\\sum_{i=1}^{8} T_i^{-1}\\left(L(T_i(x))\\right)\n$$\n\nThis detection-logit TTA already existed before 0.946. What changes in 0.946 is the representation used for temporal association. Previously, even after eight-view detection TTA, the edge predictor still received the UNet feature map from the original orientation only:\n\n$$\nF_{\\text{association}}(x) = F(x)\n$$\n\nThe 0.946 pipeline retains the UNet feature tensor from every transformed view, maps each one back to the original coordinate system, and averages them:\n\n$$\n\\bar{F}_{p}(x) = \\frac{1}{8}\\sum_{i=1}^{8} T_i^{-1}\\left(F_{p}(T_i(x))\\right)\n$$\n\nwhere the subscript $p$ denotes the primary model. The primary edge predictor therefore receives:\n\n$$\nF_{p,\\,\\text{association}}(x) = \\bar{F}_{p}(x)\n$$\n\nrather than the original-view feature representation alone. The improvement from 0.941 to 0.946 therefore comes from propagating the existing D4 ensemble farther into inference rather than adding more geometric transformations.\n\n**What's new in 0.947: completing spatial ensembling across the secondary association path.** The dual-seed pipeline already uses a secondary temporal model as a supporting signal. Before 0.947, the secondary model participates in detection ensembling and association fusion, but its feature representation used by the secondary edge predictor remains based on the original orientation. This means that after 0.946 the two association branches are asymmetric:\n\n$$\nF_{p,\\,\\text{association}}(x) = \\bar{F}_{p}(x)\n$$\n\nfor the primary model, while the secondary branch still uses:\n\n$$\nF_{s,\\,\\text{association}}(x) = F_s(x)\n$$\n\nwhere $F_s(x)$ is the secondary model's original-view feature tensor. The 0.947 configuration extends D4 feature aggregation into this secondary branch as well. The secondary model now retains and inverse-aligns its UNet feature tensor from the same eight spatial views:\n\n$$\n\\bar{F}_{s}(x) = \\frac{1}{8}\\sum_{i=1}^{8} T_i^{-1}\\left(F_s(T_i(x))\\right)\n$$\n\nUnlike the primary branch, however, the final secondary feature representation is not replaced entirely by the eight-view mean. The 0.947 configuration uses a **0.75 TTA blend weight**, preserving part of the original-view representation while giving most of the weight to the spatially ensembled representation:\n\n$$\nF_{s,\\,0.947}(x)\n=\n(1-\\lambda_s)F_s(x)\n+\n\\lambda_s\\bar{F}_s(x),\n\\;\n\\lambda_s = 0.75\n$$\n\nor equivalently,\n\n$$\nF_{s,\\,0.947}(x)\n=\n0.25F_s(x)\n+\n0.75\\bar{F}_s(x)\n$$\n\nThe secondary edge predictor then consumes this blended representation. The distinction is important: 0.947 does **not** increase the secondary edge weight itself and does **not** replace the existing low-margin consensus mechanism. It changes the spatial representation from which the secondary model produces its supporting edge evidence. The association paths therefore progress from:\n\n$$\n\\text{0.946:}\n\\,\n\\begin{cases}\n\\text{Primary edge predictor} \\leftarrow \\bar{F}_p(x)\n\\\\\n\\text{Secondary edge predictor} \\leftarrow F_s(x)\n\\end{cases}\n$$\n\nto:\n\n$$\n\\text{0.947:}\n\\,\n\\begin{cases}\n\\text{Primary edge predictor} \\leftarrow \\bar{F}_p(x)\n\\\\\n\\text{Secondary edge predictor} \\leftarrow 0.25F_s(x) + 0.75\\bar{F}_s(x)\n\\end{cases}\n$$\n\nso both temporal models now benefit from spatially ensembled feature information before their association evidence is combined.\n\n**What's new in 0.947: extending D4 TTA into the DeepCenter repair gate.** DeepCenter is not the primary detector or edge predictor. It is used as an independent learned spatial confirmation signal for selected repair decisions, including safe-division recovery. In 0.946, this gate still evaluates each frame from a single spatial orientation even though the primary detection and association paths already use D4 TTA. The 0.947 configuration applies the same eight-view D4 principle to the DeepCenter logits. For a frame $x$, let $D(T_i(x))$ denote the DeepCenter logit volume produced from spatial view $T_i$. Each output is inverse-aligned before averaging:\n\n$$\n\\bar{D}(x)\n=\n\\frac{1}{8}\n\\sum_{i=1}^{8}\nT_i^{-1}\\left(D(T_i(x))\\right)\n$$\n\nThe final DeepCenter heatmap is then obtained from the averaged logits:\n\n$$\nH_{\\text{DC}}(x)\n=\n\\sigma\\left(\\bar{D}(x)\\right)\n$$\n\nrather than applying the sigmoid to a single-view logit map. This matters because the DeepCenter score is used as a gate for repair candidates. A candidate should therefore be less dependent on the arbitrary spatial orientation of the input frame before being accepted or rejected. The DeepCenter update completes a broader consistency pattern in the inference pipeline:\n\n| Spatially Ensembled Representation | 0.946 | 0.947 |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Detection logits | on | on |\n| Primary edge features | on | on |\n| Secondary detection logits | on | on |\n| Secondary edge features | off | on |\n| DeepCenter repair logits | off | on |\n\nThe 0.947 update therefore does not introduce a new tracking architecture. It extends an already successful invariance mechanism into two branches that were still operating from single-view representations.\n\n**What's new in 0.947: safe-division confirmation threshold 0.25 → 0.20.** Alongside DeepCenter TTA, the safe-division confirmation threshold is adjusted from 0.25 to 0.20. The geometric division constraints themselves remain unchanged: the parent search radius stays at 9 µm, the sister-distance limit stays at 14 µm, the sister-symmetry gate stays at 0.6, and the existing frame and global division caps remain intact. The threshold therefore changes only the learned DeepCenter confirmation stage:\n\n$$\n\\text{accept safe-division candidate if}\n\\,\ns_{\\text{DC}} \\ge \\tau_{\\text{DC}}\n$$\n\nwith:\n\n$$\n\\tau_{\\text{DC}}:\n0.25\n\\rightarrow\n0.20\n$$\n\nin the 0.947 configuration. Because the DeepCenter score itself is now produced from an eight-view averaged logit representation, this threshold change should be interpreted together with the DeepCenter TTA update rather than as an isolated global relaxation. The geometric search space is not widened further; instead, the learned confirmation gate operates on a more spatially averaged score and uses the 0.20 acceptance threshold present in the verified 0.947 configuration. The direct functional difference can be summarized as:\n\n| Component | 0.946 Public LB | 0.947 Public LB |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Detection D4 TTA | 8 views | 8 views |\n| Primary edge-feature D4 TTA | on | on |\n| Primary edge-feature aggregation | full 8-view mean | full 8-view mean |\n| Secondary detection D4 TTA | on | on |\n| Secondary edge-feature D4 TTA | off | on |\n| Secondary edge-feature TTA blend | original view only | 0.25 original + 0.75 D4 mean |\n| DeepCenter D4 TTA | off | on |\n| DeepCenter safe-division threshold | 0.25 | 0.20 |\n| Safe division parent radius | 9.0 µm | 9.0 µm |\n| Safe division sister radius | 14.0 µm | 14.0 µm |\n| Sister symmetry gate | 0.6 | 0.6 |\n| Gap-close radius | 5.0 µm | 5.0 µm |\n| Bidirectional association weight | 0.15 | 0.15 |\n| Bidirectional fusion | harmonic probability | harmonic probability |\n| Dual-seed association framework | unchanged | unchanged |\n| ILP global linking | unchanged | unchanged |\n| Held-out post-process selection | on | on |\n\nThe important point is that **0.946 → 0.947 is not another global rewrite of linking or repair**. The primary feature-TTA path that produced 0.946 is preserved. The 0.947 configuration instead removes two remaining single-view inconsistencies: the secondary model's association features and the DeepCenter repair logits. The safe-division threshold is also adjusted from 0.25 to 0.20 as part of the verified 0.947 configuration, while the underlying division geometry and the rest of the 0.946 repair settings remain unchanged.\n\n**Summary.** The progression remains cumulative. **0.934 → 0.939** widened safe-division recovery with additional geometric and DeepCenter safeguards while making bidirectional association more conservative. **0.939 → 0.941** redistributed the repair budget by widening the parent-side division search, strengthening its DeepCenter confirmation, and tightening gap closing. **0.941 → 0.946** extended the existing eight-view D4 ensemble from detection logits into the primary UNet features consumed by the edge predictor. **0.946 → 0.947** retains that primary feature ensemble and extends the same spatial-consistency principle into the secondary edge-feature path and the DeepCenter repair gate, while changing the DeepCenter safe-division threshold from 0.25 to 0.20. The resulting verified progression is **0.933 → 0.934 → 0.939 → 0.941 → 0.946 → 0.947**. _validator_prediction_signature, 'predict_val_seconds': predict_val_seconds, 'val_stems': val_stems, 'method': val_method_prefix})\nelse:\n    _validator_prediction_signature = _resume_signature({'resume_schema': RESUME_SCHEMA_VERSION, 'disabled': True, 'val_stems': val_stems})\n\nfrom scipy.optimize import linear_sum_assignment\n\n# Match predicted and ground-truth nodes with one-to-one spatial assignment\ndef match_nodes_bipartite(pred_nodes: dict, gt_nodes: dict, max_dist: float = 7.0):\n    pred_by_t: dict[int, list[int]] = {}\n    for pid, (t, *_r) in pred_nodes.items():\n        pred_by_t.setdefault(int(t), []).append(pid)\n    gt_by_t: dict[int, list[int]] = {}\n    for gid, (t, *_r) in gt_nodes.items():\n        gt_by_t.setdefault(int(t), []).append(gid)\n    pred_to_gt: dict[int, int] = {}\n    gt_to_pred: dict[int, int] = {}\n    for t, p_ids in pred_by_t.items():\n        g_ids = gt_by_t.get(t, [])\n        if not g_ids:\n            continue\n        voxel_scale = np.array(VOXEL_SCALE_UM, dtype = float)\n        p_pos = np.array([pred_nodes[p][1:] for p in p_ids], dtype = float) * voxel_scale\n        g_pos = np.array([gt_nodes[g][1:] for g in g_ids], dtype = float) * voxel_scale\n        diff = p_pos[:, None, :] - g_pos[None, :, :]\n        cost = np.sqrt((diff ** 2).sum(axis = -1))\n        BIG = 1000000.0\n        cost_gated = np.where(cost <= max_dist, cost, BIG)\n        row_ind, col_ind = linear_sum_assignment(cost_gated)\n        for r, c in zip(row_ind, col_ind):\n            if cost_gated[r, c] >= BIG:\n                continue\n            pred_to_gt[p_ids[r]] = g_ids[c]\n            gt_to_pred[g_ids[c]] = p_ids[r]\n    return (pred_to_gt, gt_to_pred)\n\n# Compute edge true positives, false positives, and false negatives after node matching\ndef compute_edge_confusion(pred_edges, gt_edges, pred_to_gt, gt_to_pred):\n    gt_edge_set = set(gt_edges)\n    gt_outgoing: dict[int, set[int]] = {}\n    gt_incoming_source: dict[int, int] = {}\n    for s, t in gt_edge_set:\n        gt_outgoing.setdefault(s, set()).add(t)\n        gt_incoming_source[t] = s\n    tp = 0\n    fp = 0\n    matched_gt_edges = set()\n    for s, t in pred_edges:\n        ms = pred_to_gt.get(s)\n        mt = pred_to_gt.get(t)\n        is_tp = ms is not None and mt is not None and (mt in gt_outgoing.get(ms, ()))\n        if is_tp:\n            tp += 1\n            matched_gt_edges.add((ms, mt))\n            continue\n        is_fp = mt is not None and mt in gt_incoming_source or (ms is not None and bool(gt_outgoing.get(ms)))\n        if is_fp:\n            fp += 1\n    fn = len(gt_edge_set - matched_gt_edges)\n    return (tp, fp, fn)\n\n# Compute the edge jaccard component of the validator metric\ndef edge_jaccard(tp: int, fp: int, fn: int) -> float:\n    denom = tp + fp + fn\n    return tp / denom if denom else 0.0\n\n# Apply the node-count penalty to the edge jaccard score\ndef adjusted_jaccard(jaccard: float, t_pred: int, t_true, a: float = 0.1) -> float:\n    if not t_true or t_true <= 0:\n        return jaccard\n    return max(0.0, jaccard * (1.0 - a * (t_pred - t_true) / t_true))\n\n# Build weakly connected components for patched division matching\ndef weakly_connected_components(node_ids, edges):\n    parent = {n: n for n in node_ids}\n\n    # Find the current disjoint-set representative\n    def find(x):\n        while parent[x] != x:\n            parent[x] = parent[parent[x]]\n            x = parent[x]\n        return x\n\n    # Merge two disjoint-set components\n    def union(a, b):\n        ra, rb = (find(a), find(b))\n        if ra != rb:\n            parent[ra] = rb\n    for s, t in edges:\n        if s in parent and t in parent:\n            union(s, t)\n    return {n: find(n) for n in node_ids}\n\n# Compute division true positives, false positives, and false negatives\ndef compute_division_confusion(pred_nodes, pred_edges, gt_nodes, gt_edges, pred_to_gt, gt_to_pred):\n    gt_out: dict[int, set[int]] = {}\n    gt_in: dict[int, int] = {}\n    for s, t in gt_edges:\n        gt_out.setdefault(s, set()).add(t)\n        gt_in[t] = s\n    pred_out: dict[int, set[int]] = {}\n    for s, t in pred_edges:\n        pred_out.setdefault(s, set()).add(t)\n    pred_node_ids = list(pred_nodes.keys())\n    pred_edge_list = list(pred_edges)\n    components = weakly_connected_components(pred_node_ids, pred_edge_list)\n    fork_components = {components[n] for n, outs in pred_out.items() if len(outs) >= 2 and n in components}\n    gt_division_sources = [s for s, outs in gt_out.items() if len(outs) >= 2]\n\n    # Collect lineage descendants used by patched division matching\n    def lineage_descendants(root_child: int) -> set[int]:\n        seen = {root_child}\n        stack = [root_child]\n        while stack:\n            cur = stack.pop()\n            for nxt in gt_out.get(cur, ()):\n                if nxt not in seen:\n                    seen.add(nxt)\n                    stack.append(nxt)\n        return seen\n    tp = 0\n    fn = 0\n    tp_gt_sources: set[int] = set()\n    for gsrc in gt_division_sources:\n        children = sorted(gt_out[gsrc])\n        if len(children) < 2:\n            continue\n        anchor_candidates = [gsrc]\n        if gsrc in gt_in:\n            anchor_candidates.append(gt_in[gsrc])\n        anchor_pred_nodes = [gt_to_pred[a] for a in anchor_candidates if a in gt_to_pred]\n        lineage_hit_components: list[set[int]] = []\n        ok = True\n        for child in children[:2]:\n            lineage = lineage_descendants(child)\n            hit_comp_ids = {components[p_id] for gt_id in lineage if (p_id := gt_to_pred.get(gt_id)) is not None and p_id in components}\n            if not hit_comp_ids:\n                ok = False\n                break\n            lineage_hit_components.append(hit_comp_ids)\n        if not ok or not anchor_pred_nodes:\n            fn += 1\n            continue\n        anchor_comp_ids = {components[p] for p in anchor_pred_nodes if p in components}\n        if not anchor_comp_ids:\n            fn += 1\n            continue\n        found = any((comp_id in lineage_hit_components[0] and comp_id in lineage_hit_components[1] and (comp_id in fork_components) for comp_id in anchor_comp_ids))\n        if found:\n            tp += 1\n            tp_gt_sources.add(gsrc)\n        else:\n            fn += 1\n    fp = 0\n    for n, outs in pred_out.items():\n        if len(outs) < 2:\n            continue\n        g = pred_to_gt.get(n)\n        if g is None or g not in gt_out or g in tp_gt_sources:\n            continue\n        fp += 1\n    return (tp, fp, fn)\n\n# Decompose validator errors into the official metric components\ndef decompose_errors(pred_nodes, gt_nodes, pred_edges, gt_edges, pred_to_gt, gt_to_pred):\n    gt_edge_set = set(gt_edges)\n    pred_edge_set = set(pred_edges)\n    gt_outgoing: dict[int, set[int]] = {}\n    for s, t in gt_edge_set:\n        gt_outgoing.setdefault(s, set()).add(t)\n    missed_gt_nodes = sum((1 for g in gt_nodes if g not in gt_to_pred))\n    spurious_pred_nodes = sum((1 for p in pred_nodes if p not in pred_to_gt))\n    recovered = fragmented = lost_to_detection = 0\n    for gs, gtid in gt_edge_set:\n        ps, pt = (gt_to_pred.get(gs), gt_to_pred.get(gtid))\n        if ps is None or pt is None:\n            lost_to_detection += 1\n        elif (ps, pt) in pred_edge_set:\n            recovered += 1\n        else:\n            fragmented += 1\n    wrong_association = 0\n    for ps, pt in pred_edge_set:\n        ms, mt = (pred_to_gt.get(ps), pred_to_gt.get(pt))\n        if ms is not None and mt is not None and (mt not in gt_outgoing.get(ms, ())):\n            wrong_association += 1\n    return {'missed_gt_nodes': missed_gt_nodes, 'spurious_pred_nodes': spurious_pred_nodes, 'edges_recovered': recovered, 'edges_fragmented': fragmented, 'edges_lost_to_detection': lost_to_detection, 'wrong_association_edges': wrong_association}\n\n# Read a nested metadata key from the ground-truth geff payload\ndef _find_key_recursive(obj, key):\n    if isinstance(obj, dict):\n        if key in obj:\n            return obj[key]\n        for v in obj.values():\n            found = _find_key_recursive(v, key)\n            if found is not None:\n                return found\n    elif isinstance(obj, list):\n        for item in obj:\n            found = _find_key_recursive(item, key)\n            if found is not None:\n                return found\n    return None\n\n# Read the estimated true node count used by the metric penalty\ndef read_estimated_true_node_count(geff_path: Path):\n    for candidate in (geff_path / 'zarr.json', geff_path / '.zattrs'):\n        if not candidate.exists():\n            continue\n        try:\n            payload = json.loads(candidate.read_text())\n        except Exception:\n            continue\n        found = _find_key_recursive(payload, 'estimated_number_of_nodes')\n        if found is not None:\n            try:\n                return float(found)\n            except (TypeError, ValueError):\n                continue\n    return None\n\n# Convert a geff graph into plain node and edge structures\ndef graph_to_plain(graph):\n    nodes: dict[int, tuple] = {}\n    for row in graph.node_attrs().iter_rows(named = True):\n        node_id = int(row['node_id'])\n        nodes[node_id] = (int(row['t']), float(row['z']), float(row['y']), float(row['x']))\n    edges: list[tuple[int, int]] = []\n    for row in graph.edge_attrs().iter_rows(named = True):\n        edges.append((int(row['source_id']), int(row['target_id'])))\n    return (nodes, edges)\n\n# Convert processed node dictionaries into validator node tuples\ndef nodes_by_id_to_plain(nodes_by_id):\n match_nodes_bipartite(pred_nodes: dict, gt_nodes: dict, max_dist: float = 7.0):\n    pred_by_t: dict[int, list[int]] = {}\n    for pid, (t, *_r) in pred_nodes.items():\n        pred_by_t.setdefault(int(t), []).append(pid)\n    gt_by_t: dict[int, list[int]] = {}\n    for gid, (t, *_r) in gt_nodes.items():\n        gt_by_t.setdefault(int(t), []).append(gid)\n\n    pred_to_gt:      row_ind, col_ind = linear_sum_assignment(cost_gated)\n        for r, c in zip(row_ind, col_ind):\n            if cost_gated[r, c] >= BIG:\n                continue\n weakly_connected_components(node_ids, edges):\n    parent = {n: n for n in node_ids}\n\n    def find(x):\n        while parent[x] != x:\n            parent[x] = parent[parent[x]]\n            x = parent[x]\n        return x\n\n    def union(a, b):\n        ra, rb = find(a), find(b)\n        if ra != rb:\n            parent[ra] = rb\n\n    for s, t in edges:\n        if s in parent and t in \"missed_gt_nodes\": missed_gt_nodes,\n        \"spurious_pred_nodes\": spurious_pred_nodes,\n        \"edges_recovered\": recovered,\n        \"edges_fragmented\": fragmented,\n ILP tracker with the selected detection threshold and stricter graph-repair caps.\n\nPipeline summary:\n\n- **Center model:** `TemporalUNet3D` predicts cell-center logits from short 3D time windows.\n- **Edge model:** a node cross-attention transformer scores candidate parent-child links between adjacent frames.\n- **Graph optimizer:** an ILP selects a sparse tracking graph from learned edge scores and event costs.\n- **Deterministic repair:** physical-motion relinking, bounded gap repair, conservative division recovery, and line-fit coordinate smoothing.\n\nThis variant keeps the selected detection threshold and applies stricter graph-repair caps.","metadata":{}},{"id":"672fef79-a813-46f6-89e1-c5832b05240e","cell_type":"markdown","source":"## Current Model and Submission Logic\n\nThe submitted graph is produced by a single learned tracker artifact followed by geometry-constrained graph repair.\n\n**Learned / optimization components**\n\n- `TemporalUNet3D` center detector: predicts cell-center logits from short 3D time windows.\n- Node cross-attention edge predictor: scores candidate parent-child links between adjacent frames.\n- ILP graph constructor: selects a sparse tracking graph from learned edge scores and event costs.\n\n**Deterministic post-processing**\n\n- Physical-motion relinking.\n- Bounded one-frame and two-frame gap repair.\n- Conservative division recovery.\n- Topology-preserving line-fit coordinate smoothing.\n\nThis profile keeps the selected detection threshold while further reducing synthetic gap, gap2, and division repair for a sharper checkpoint.\n\n### Training Objective\n\nFor a short temporal window, the model encodes the downsampled 3D volumes with a\n`TemporalUNet3D` encoder. The encoder output at frame $t$ is converted into a\ncenter logit field by a $1\\times1\\times1$ convolution.\n\n$$\nF_t = h_\\theta(V_{t:t+W-1})_t,\n\\qquad\n a_t(\\mathbf r) = q_\\theta(F_t(\\mathbf r)),\n\\qquad\np_t(\\mathbf r)=\\sigma(a_t(\\mathbf r)).\n$$\n\nGround-truth node voxels are positives and all other voxels are weak negatives.\nFor one frame, the detection target is $y_t(\\mathbf r)\\in\\{0,1\\}$. The per-sample\nweights normalize positive and negative mass separately:\n\n$$\nw_+(b)=\\frac{1}{N_+(b)},\n\\qquad\nw_-(b)=\\frac{\\alpha}{N_-(b)},\n\\qquad \\alpha=0.01.\n$$\n\nThe detection loss is weighted binary cross entropy on logits:\n\n$$\n\\mathcal L_{\\mathrm{det}}\n=\n\\frac{1}{B}\\sum_{b=1}^{B}\\sum_{\\mathbf r}\n w_b(\\mathbf r)\n\\,\\mathrm{BCELogit}(a_b(\\mathbf r),y_b(\\mathbf r)).\n$$\n\nLocal maxima of $p_t$ become candidate detections. For consecutive frames, node\nfeatures are sampled from the UNet feature maps and passed through a bidirectional\ncross-attention transformer. The edge logit from source node $i$ to target node\n$j$ is\n\n$$\n\\ell_{ij}=g_\\phi\\left([F_t(\\mathbf r_i),\\psi(\\mathbf r_i,t)],\n[F_{t+1}(\\mathbf r_j),\\psi(\\mathbf r_j,t+1)],\n\\mathbf r_j-\\mathbf r_i\\right).\n$$\n\nDuring training, edge probabilities are normalized over possible parents of each\ntarget:\n\n$$\nP_{ij}=\\mathrm{softmax}_{i}(\\ell_{ij}).\n$$\n\nThis permits one parent to connect to two daughters while discouraging many\nparents for the same target. Because annotations are sparse, the edge loss is\ncomputed only on rows or columns that touch an annotated edge:\n\n$$\n\\mathcal M_{ij}=1\n\\quad\\mathrm{if}\\quad\n\\sum_j y_{ij}>0\\quad\\mathrm{or}\\quad\\sum_i y_{ij}>0.\n$$\n\nThe edge objective is focal-style binary cross entropy:\n\n$$\n\\mathcal L_{\\mathrm{edge}}\n=\n\\mathrm{mean}_{(i,j):\\mathcal M_{ij}=1}\n(1-P^{*}_{ij})^2\\,\\mathrm{BCE}(P_{ij},y_{ij}),\n$$\n\nwhere $P^{*}_{ij}=P_{ij}$ when $y_{ij}=1$ and $P^{*}_{ij}=1-P_{ij}$ otherwise.\nThe trained checkpoint minimizes\n\n$$\n\\mathcal L\n=\n\\mathcal L_{\\mathrm{edge}}\n+\\lambda_{\\mathrm{det}}\\mathcal L_{\\mathrm{det}},\n\\qquad \\lambda_{\\mathrm{det}}=1.\n$$\n\n### Submission Graph Construction\n\nAt inference time, detections are local maxima above the fixed probability\nthreshold $\\tau=0.985$. Candidate links come from the learned edge predictor and\nare solved with the ILP settings in `RUN_CONFIG`.\n\nAll geometry after prediction is measured in microns:\n\n$$\nd_{\\mu\\mathrm{m}}(i,j)=\n\\sqrt{(1.625\\Delta z)^2+(0.40625\\Delta y)^2+(0.40625\\Delta x)^2}.\n$$\n\nThe motion relinker rebuilds one-step temporal links from detected nodes. If a\nnode has a predecessor, its next position is extrapolated by\n\n$$\n\\hat{\\mathbf r}_{i,t+1}=\\mathbf r_{i,t}\n+\\lambda_v(\\mathbf r_{i,t}-\\mathbf r_{i,t-1}).\n$$\n\nA Hungarian assignment is then solved with cost\n\n$$\nC_{ij}=d_{\\mathrm{motion}}(i,j)+0.05d_{\\mathrm{raw}}(i,j)-\\beta P_{ij}^{\\mathrm{learned}}.\n$$\n\nThis notebook uses\n\n$$\n\\lambda_v=0.52,\\qquad\n\\beta=0.78,\\qquad\nR_{\\mathrm{tight}}=6.2\\,\\mu\\mathrm{m},\\qquad\nR_{\\mathrm{relaxed}}=10.4\\,\\mu\\mathrm{m}.\n$$\n\nOne-frame gap repair can insert or reuse a middle-frame node when a track end at\n$t$ and a track start at $t+2$ are physically close enough:\n\n$$\nd_{\\mu\\mathrm{m}}(i,j)\\le 2g,\n\\qquad g=5.75\\,\\mu\\mathrm{m}.\n$$\n\nTwo-missing-frame recovery is controlled by a much smaller cap. When enabled,\nit requires\n\n$$\nd_{\\mu\\mathrm{m}}(i,j)\\le R_2,\n\\qquad\n\\frac{d_{\\mu\\mathrm{m}}(i,j)}{3}\\le s_2,\n$$\n\nwith\n\n$$\nR_2=9.7\\,\\mu\\mathrm{m},\n\\qquad\ns_2=4.05\\,\\mu\\mathrm{m},\n\\qquad\n\\rho_2=0.0032.\n$$\n\nFinally, line-fit smoothing modifies only coordinates, not graph topology. For a\nlinear local track neighbourhood,\n\n$$\n\\mathbf r'_i=(1-w)\\mathbf r_i+w\\,\\mathrm{LineFit}_{\\mathcal N(i)}(t_i),\n\\qquad w=0.76.\n$$\n\nThe submission writer emits only the required node and edge rows and validates\nthat every hidden-test dataset appears in `submission.csv`.","metadata":{}},{"id":"0702efd6-dbfb-4176-89e3-410139ed55eb","cell_type":"code","source":"from __future__ Just before it, at t = 22 to 24, the parent condenses into a short bright band. Just after it, the two daughters look fainter than the parent did. It is tempting to read that second part as the cell dimming.\n\nThat is where I went wrong, so it is worth measuring rather than believing.\n\n## Chapter 4 &middot; What \"fading\" actually means\n\nMy first measurement was mean intensity in a fixed-radius ball at each annotated position. It showed dividing cells dropping to 0.84 of their starting value while ordinary cells stayed flat, which looked like a clean result.\n\nIt was an artefact of the ruler. A fixed-radius ball around a **smaller** object contains more background, so the mean falls even when nothing gets dimmer.\n\nThe fix is to measure three things in the same box instead of one:\n\n| quantity | what it is | what it tracks |\n|---|---|---|\n| **peak** | brightest voxel above the local background | brightness, nearly independent of size |\n| **volume** | voxels above halfway between background and peak | **size** |\n| **mean** | the naive measure | a mixture of the two |\n\nIf volume falls while peak holds, the nucleus got smaller and did not get dimmer.\n\nThe control is paired: for each division, up to three ordinary single-child tracks **from the same film starting on the same frame**. Anything that drifts across a film, bleaching or focus, then hits both arms equally and cancels.\n\nOne more thing had to change before the numbers meant anything. Reading label graphs is cheap and reading image volumes is not, so my first run simply took the first 40 films. It found 5 divisions and every interval covered zero. The cell below surveys all 199 graphs first and spends the volume budget on the films that actually carry divisions."},{"cell_type":"code","metadata":{},"execution_count":null,"outputs":[],"source":"RADIUS, WINDOW = 5, 6\n\ndef probe(vol, z, y, x):\n    \"\"\"Three numbers from one small box, which is the whole point of this cell.\n\n      peak   - brightest voxel above the local background. No interval, no claim.\"\"\"\n    obs = np.median(a[:, k]) - np.median(b[:, k])\n    s = np.array([np.median(rng.choice(a[:, k], len(a))) - np.median(rng.choice(b[:, k], len(b)))\n                  for _ in range(n)])\n    return obs, *np.percentile(s, [2.5, 97.5])\n\nfig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(13.5, 4.1), sharex=True)\npanels = [('volume  (size)', DV, CV, '#c0392b'),\n          ('peak  (brightness)', DP, CP, '#2471a3'),\n          ('mean  (the naive one)', DM, CM, '#7d6608')]\nfor ax, (title, A, B, col) in zip(axes, panels):\n    for arr, lab, c in ((B, 'ordinary', '#7f8c8d'), (A, 'dividing', col)):\n        med = np.median(arr, 0)\n        ax.fill_between(lags, np.percentile(arr, 25, 0), np.percentile(arr, 75, 0),\n                        color=c, alpha=0.15)\n        ax.plot(lags, med, color=c, lw=2.2, marker='o', ms=3.5, label=lab)\n    ax.axvline(0, color='#b8860b', lw=1.1, ls='--')\n    ax.axhline(1.0, color='#bbbbbb', lw=0.8)\n    ax.set_title(title); ax.set_xlabel('frames from the division'); ax.grid(alpha=0.28)\n    ax.legend(fontsize=9)\naxes[0].set_ylabel('relative to the track start')\nfig.suptitle('A dividing nucleus gets smaller, not dimmer', y=1.02, fontsize=13)\nfig.tight_layout()\nplt.show()\n\nfor name, A, B in (('VOLUME', DV, CV), ('PEAK', DP, CP), ('MEAN', DM, CM)):\n    print(f'\\n{name}   dividing minus ordinary, 95% bootstrap interval')\n    for k, dt in enumerate(lags):\n        if dt < -2:\n            continue\n        o, lo_, hi_ = boot(A, B, k)\n        flag = '  <-- clears zero' if (lo_ > 0 or hi_ < 0) else ''\n        print(f'   dt={dt:+d}   {o:+6.3f}  [{lo_:+.3f}, {hi_:+.3f}]{flag}')"},{"cell_type":"markdown","metadata":{},"source":"## Chapter 6 &middot; Reading it\n\nThe three panels disagree, and the disagreement is the finding.\n\n**Volume** is down, and its intervals clear zero at seven of the nine lags shown: at -2 and -1 before the division (the -1 bound only just), then +1 through +5 after it. The deepest point is about `-0.27` at three frames after the division, and by +6 it is drifting back toward the controls.\n\n**Peak** is not. Its only lag that clears zero is the division frame itself, where the nucleus is mid-split. At every lag after that the interval covers zero: the daughters are as bright as the parent was.\n\n**Mean** falls and stays down from +1 through +6, which is what my first version measured and mistook for dimming. It was reading the volume drop through a fixed-size probe.\n\nSo a dividing nucleus is **smaller**, not dimmer, and the apparent fade in the animation is mostly geometry.\n\nSmaller after the split is expected on its own: each daughter carries half of the parent's chromatin. Two parts of the result are not automatic.\n\n**Brightness is kept.** Half the material in a smaller nucleus leaves the peak where it was, rather than halving it.\n\n**The size change starts before the split.** Volume is already below the controls at -2 and -1. That is consistent with the chromatin condensing ahead of the division, which is what the bright band at t = 22 to 24 in the animation looks like, although a box measurement cannot separate condensation from other causes.\n\nThe effect is a window rather than a step: it peaks around +3 and is fading by +6. The frames that decide the division half of the metric, the split and the one after it, fall inside that window.\n\nThese numbers are relative to each track's own start. They say nothing against dividing nuclei being brighter than ordinary ones in absolute terms, which is a comparison between cells rather than over time.\n\nCaveats I would want stated if I were reading this:\n\n- The film budget is bounded and printed. It reads the division-richest films, so these divisions are not a uniform sample of all of them.\n- Half-max volume in a small box is a crude size estimate on an anisotropic voxel grid (1.625 by 0.40625 by 0.40625 micrometres). It is good enough to separate size from brightness, which is all it is asked to do here, and not good enough to quote as a nuclear volume.\n- The intervals are per-lag and uncorrected. Volume clearing zero at seven lags in a row is not something to read one lag at a time, but a single isolated lag elsewhere would not be worth much.\n\nThe animation is written to `/kaggle/working/division.gif` if you want to reuse it.\n"}],"metadata":{"kernelspec":{"display_name":"Python 3","language":"python","name":"python3"},"language_info":{"name":"python"}},"nbformat":4,"nbformat_minor":5}

============================================================\n# CELL 9 (NEW) -- VALIDATOR: scoring against the official metric\n# (https://github.com/royerlab/kaggle-cell-tracking-competition/blob/main/metrics.md)\n# Division-matching reflects the organizers' post-exploit patch (single\n# connected component + both-daughter-lineage coverage + anchor + fork).\n# ============================================================\n\nfrom scipy.optimize import linear_sum_assignment\n\n\ndef match_nodes_bipartite(pred_nodes: dict, gt_nodes: dict, max_dist: float = 7.0):\n    pred_by_t: dict[int, list[int]] = {}\n    for pid, (t, *_r) in pred_nodes.items():\n        pred_by_t.setdefault(int(t), []).append(pid)\n    gt_by_t: dict[int, list[int]] = {}\n    for gid, (t, *_r) in gt_nodes.items():\n        gt_by_t.setdefault(int(t), []).append(gid)\n\n    pred_to_gt: dict[int, int] = {}\n    gt_to_pred: dict[int, int] = {}\n    for t, p_ids in pred_by_t.items():\n        g_ids = gt_by_t.get(t, [])\n        if not g_ids:\n            continue\n        voxel_scale = np.array(VOXEL_SCALE_UM, dtype=float)\n        p_pos = np.array([pred_nodes[p][1:] for p in p_ids], dtype=float) * voxel_scale\n        g_pos = np.array([gt_nodes[g][1:] for g in g_ids], dtype=float) * voxel_scale\n        diff = p_pos[:, None, :] - g_pos[None, :, :]\n        cost = np.sqrt((diff ** 2).sum(axis=-1))\n        BIG = 1e6\n        cost_gated = np.where(cost <= max_dist, cost, BIG)\n        row_ind, col_ind = linear_sum_assignment(cost_gated)\n        for r, c in zip(row_ind, col_ind):\n            if cost_gated[r, c] >= BIG:\n                continue\n            pred_to_gt[p_ids[r]] = g_ids[c]\n            gt_to_pred[g_ids[c]] = p_ids[r]\n    return pred_to_gt, gt_to_pred\n\n\ndef compute_edge_confusion(pred_edges, gt_edges, pred_to_gt, gt_to_pred):\n ============================================================\n# CELL 9 (NEW) -- VALIDATOR: scoring against the official metric\n# (https://github.com/royerlab/kaggle-cell-tracking-competition/blob/main/metrics.md)\n# Division-matching reflects the organizers' post-exploit patch (single\n# connected component + both-daughter-lineage coverage + anchor + fork).\n# ============================================================\n\nfrom scipy.optimize import linear_sum_assignment\n\n\ndef match_nodes_bipartite(pred_nodes: dict, gt_nodes: dict, max_dist: float = 7.0):\n    pred_by_t: dict[int, list[int]] = {}\n    for pid, (t, *_r) in pred_nodes.items():\n        pred_by_t.setdefault(int(t), []).append(pid)\n    gt_by_t: dict[int, list[int]] = {}\n    for gid, (t, *_r) in gt_nodes.items():\n        gt_by_t.setdefault(int(t), []).append(gid)\n\n    pred_to_gt: dict[int, int] = {}\n    gt_to_pred: dict[int, int] = {}\n    for t, p_ids in pred_by_t.items():\n        g_ids = gt_by_t.get(t, [])\n        if not g_ids:\n            continue\n        voxel_scale = np.array(VOXEL_SCALE_UM, dtype=float)\n        p_pos = np.array([pred_nodes[p][1:] for p in p_ids], dtype=float) * voxel_scale\n        g_pos = np.array([gt_nodes[g][1:] for g in g_ids], dtype=float) * voxel_scale\n        diff = p_pos[:, None, :] - g_pos[None, :, :]\n        cost = np.sqrt((diff ** 2).sum(axis=-1))\n        BIG = 1e6\n        cost_gated = np.where(cost <= max_dist, cost, BIG)\n        row_ind, col_ind = linear_sum_assignment(cost_gated)\n        for r, c in zip(row_ind, col_ind):\n            if cost_gated[r, c] >= BIG:\n                continue\n            pred_to_gt[p_ids[r]] = g_ids[c]\n            gt_to_pred[g_ids[c]] = p_ids[r]\n    return pred_to_gt, gt_to_pred\n\n\ndef compute_edge_confusion(pred_edges, gt_edges, pred_to_gt, gt_to_pred):\n ============================================================\n# CELL 9 (NEW) -- VALIDATOR: scoring against the official metric\n# (https://github.com/royerlab/kaggle-cell-tracking-competition/blob/main/metrics.md)\n# Division-matching reflects the organizers' post-exploit patch (single\n# connected component + both-daughter-lineage coverage + anchor + fork).\n# ============================================================\n\nfrom scipy.optimize import linear_sum_assignment\n\n\ndef match_nodes_bipartite(pred_nodes: dict, gt_nodes: dict, max_dist: float = 7.0):\n    pred_by_t: dict[int, list[int]] = {}\n    for pid, (t, *_r) in pred_nodes.items():\n        pred_by_t.setdefault(int(t), []).append(pid)\n    gt_by_t: dict[int, list[int]] = {}\n    for gid, (t, *_r) in gt_nodes.items():\n        gt_by_t.setdefault(int(t), []).append(gid)\n\n    pred_to_gt: dict[int, int] = {}\n    gt_to_pred: dict[int, int] = {}\n    for t, p_ids in pred_by_t.items():\n        g_ids = gt_by_t.get(t, [])\n        if not g_ids:\n            continue\n        voxel_scale = np.array(VOXEL_SCALE_UM, dtype=float)\n        p_pos = np.array([pred_nodes[p][1:] for p in p_ids], dtype=float) * voxel_scale\n        g_pos = np.array([gt_nodes[g][1:] for g in g_ids], dtype=float) * voxel_scale\n        diff = p_pos[:, None, :] - g_pos[None, :, :]\n        cost = np.sqrt((diff ** 2).sum(axis=-1))\n        BIG = 1e6\n        cost_gated = np.where(cost <= max_dist, cost, BIG)\n        row_ind, col_ind = linear_sum_assignment(cost_gated)\n        for r, c in zip(row_ind, col_ind):\n            if cost_gated[r, c] >= BIG:\n                continue\n            pred_to_gt[p_ids[r]] = g_ids[c]\n            gt_to_pred[g_ids[c]] = p_ids[r]\n    return pred_to_gt, gt_to_pred\n\n\ndef compute_edge_confusion(pred_edges, gt_edges, pred_to_gt, gt_to_pred):\n ============================================================\n# CELL 9 (NEW) -- VALIDATOR: scoring against the official metric\n# (https://github.com/royerlab/kaggle-cell-tracking-competition/blob/main/metrics.md)\n# Division-matching reflects the organizers' post-exploit patch (single\n# connected component + both-daughter-lineage coverage + anchor + fork).\n# ============================================================\n\nfrom scipy.optimize import linear_sum_assignment\n\n\ndef match_nodes_bipartite(pred_nodes: dict, gt_nodes: dict, max_dist: float = 7.0):\n    pred_by_t: dict[int, list[int]] = {}\n    for pid, (t, *_r) in pred_nodes.items():\n        pred_by_t.setdefault(int(t), []).append(pid)\n    gt_by_t: dict[int, list[int]] = {}\n    for gid, (t, *_r) in gt_nodes.items():\n        gt_by_t.setdefault(int(t), []).append(gid)\n\n    pred_to_gt: dict[int, int] = {}\n    gt_to_pred: dict[int, int] = {}\n    for t, p_ids in pred_by_t.items():\n        g_ids = gt_by_t.get(t, [])\n        if not g_ids:\n            continue\n        voxel_scale = np.array(VOXEL_SCALE_UM, dtype=float)\n        p_pos = np.array([pred_nodes[p][1:] for p in p_ids], dtype=float) * voxel_scale\n        g_pos = np.array([gt_nodes[g][1:] for g in g_ids], dtype=float) * voxel_scale\n        diff = p_pos[:, None, :] - g_pos[None, :, :]\n        cost = np.sqrt((diff ** 2).sum(axis=-1))\n        BIG = 1e6\n        cost_gated = np.where(cost <= max_dist, cost, BIG)\n        row_ind, col_ind = linear_sum_assignment(cost_gated)\n        for r, c in zip(row_ind, col_ind):\n            if cost_gated[r, c] >= BIG:\n                continue\n            pred_to_gt[p_ids[r]] = g_ids[c]\n            gt_to_pred[g_ids[c]] = p_ids[r]\n    return pred_to_gt, gt_to_pred\n\n\ndef compute_edge_confusion(pred_edges, gt_edges, pred_to_gt, gt_to_pred):\n
